questions.text: Describe the structure of ecosystem. Ans: Structure of ecosystem: The structure of an ecosystem can be split into two main components, namely: Biotic Components and Abiotic Components. Biotic structure includes plants, animals & microorganisms present in an ecosystem. These organisms have different nutritional behavior and status in the ecosystem and are known as Autotrophs (Producers), Heterotrophs (Consumers) & Micro-consumers (Decomposers) based on how they get their food. Abiotic components are the non-living component of an ecosystem. It includes air, water, soil, minerals, sunlight, temperature, nutrients, wind, altitude, turbidity, etc. b) Write the impact of overutilization of groundwater. Ans. Impact of overutilization of groundwater. Over use of groundwater has following effects……

Lowering of water table: Excessive use of ground water for drinking, irrigation and domestic purposes has resulted in rapid depletion of ground water in various regions leading to lowering of water table.

Ground subsidence When ground water withdrawal is greater than its recharge rate, the sediments in the aquifer become compacted. This is called ground subsidence which may cause damage of buildings, destroy water supply systems etc.
Intrusion of salt water In coastal area, over exploitation of ground water leads to rapid intrusion of salt water from the sea. As a result, water canno t be used for drinking and agriculture.
Earthquake and landslides Over-utilization of ground water r leads to decrease in water level causing earth qu uake and landslides.
Drying of well Excess withdrawal of ground wa ater, result depletion of ground water level and dr rying up of the well.

Pollution of water: When the gr water level near agr ricultural land decreases, water containing fertiliz zers percolate rapidly into the aquifer r and pollute ground water. As a result water beco omes unsuitable for drinking.

Why the pyramid of ener rgy always takes upright shape? Ans: Pyramid of Energy It shows the energy available at each trophic level. The size of each trophic level rep presents the proportion of productivity It is measured in Joules or Calor ries. Most of the energy available to t the community is in the 1 st trophic level. Only 10-20% of the energy is av vailable to the next trophic level (≈ 90% lost) Pyramid of energy is the on nly type of ecological pyramid, which is alwa ys upright, because the energy y flow in a food chain is always unidirectiona l. Also, with every increasing trophic level, some energy is lost into the envi ironment as heat energy. So if we represent any ecosy ystem food chain in terms of the energy, the val lue will always decrease from produ ucer to higher trophic levels. How N 2 cycle maintain proper functioning of the ecosystem? Ans. Nitrogen cycle Nitrogen cycle is that biogeochemical cycle through which the movement of nitrogen occurs between biotic (living) and abiotic (lithosphere, hydrosphere, atmosphere) components of the ecosystem. Process of Nitrogen Cycle consists of the following steps.. 1. Nitrogen fixation: Nitrogen from the atmosphere is converted into ammonia and other nitrogeneous compound by certain bacterial species like Rhizobium, Azotobacter, etc. and by other natural phenomena. 1. Assimilation: Nitrogen in the form of nitrite ions, nitrate ions or ammonium ions enters in the plant and animal body. 2. Ammonification: After the death of plants and animals nitrogen present in organic matter converts to ammonium compounds by ammonifying bacteria, 3. Nitrification: Nitrites and nitrate salts are formed by the oxidation of ammonia with the help of Nitrosomonas bacteria species. 4. Define biodiversity. Give various levels of biodiversity. Ans. Biodiversity is the variety and variability of life on Earth. It means "the existence of a large number of different kinds of animals and plants which make a balanced environment" Biodiversity is usually considered at three different levels……. 1. Genetic diversity The variety of genes within a given species 2. Species diversity The variety of species in a given ecosystem. Diversity is greatest when all the species present are equally abundant in the area. A large number of plants, animals and microorganisms interact with each other in a ecosystem. 3. Ecosystem diversity The variety of ecosystem in a given region Ecosystem diversity deals with the variations in ecosystems within a geographical location and its overall impact on human existence and the environment. An example of ecological diversity on a global scale would be the variation in ecosystems, such as deserts, forests, grasslands, wetlands and oceans. b) Why food web is more important ecologically than the concept of simple food chain. Ans. The transfer of food energy from the producers (plants) through a series of organisms (Herbivores, Carnivores) successively with the repeated activities of eating and being eaten is known as food chain. Whereas food web is a network of food chains where different types of organisms are connected at different trophic levels so that there are a number of options of eating and being eaten at each trophic level. So, food webs improve the stability of an ecosystem as it includes all the interconnected food chains. These webs are important for illustrating the feeding relationships in a community among the species. A food chain is a linear sequence of organisms through which food and its contained energy pass. If one of the organisms number decreases in a linear food chain, next organisms will be affected due to food shortage. However, in a food web, each organism has a choice to feed on different types of other organisms. So, the concept of the food web is more significant that food chain.

Discuss various values of biodiversity. Ans. Various values of biodiversity (i) Consumptive values, (ii) Productive use value Many industries are built depending on the productive used value of biodiversity. For e.g. industries like paper, pulp, plywood, textile, leather, pearl etc. (iii) Social value (iv) Ethical value Ethical and moral value is based on the importance of protecting all forms of life. It involves ethical issues like ''All life must be preserved'' The ethical value means that a species may or may not be used, but its existence in our nature gives us pleasure. Ex: 1. The river Ganga is considered as holy river. 2. Vembu, Tulsi are some of the trees worshipped by the Tamilans. 3. We are not deriving anything from Kangaroo, Zebra, but we feel that these should exist in nature. (v) Aesthetic value The beautiful nature of plants & animals insist us to protect the biodiversity. Ex: People from far and wide spend a lot of time and money to visit beautiful areas where they can enjoy the aesthetic value of biodiversity and this type of tourism is now known as ecotourism. The pleasant music of world birds, colour of flowers, peacock, and butterfly are important aesthetic value. (vi) Option value It includes the potential of biodiversity that are presently unknown and need to be explored. The optional values of biodiversity suggest that any species may be proved to be a valuable after someday. (i.e., presently unknown but need to be known) Eg., growing Biotechnology field is searching a species which can cure diseases like cancer and AIDS. b) What are alternative energy resources? How it fulfill the future energy need. Ans. The energy resources that can be regenerated easily through natural process once they are used up are called the renewable or alternative energy resources. Renewable energy resources include solar energy, wind power, hydropower etc. As the conventional fossil fuel energies like coal, petroleum, natural gas and nuclear energy are not abundant and one day will be exhausted, so we should depend more on the alternative non-conventional energy resources. The advantages of alternative energies are (i) They are plenty in sources (ii) Non-polluting and eco-friendly These types of energy can fulfill our future energy demand.
